sanskrit_verse: गृहम् आगत्य या नारी प्रलोभ्य स्पर्शनादिना । कामयेत तत्र सा दण्ड्या नरस्यार्धदमः स्मृतः ॥
transliteration: gṛham āgatya yā nārī pralobhya sparśanādinā / kāmayet tatra sā daṇḍyā narasyārdhadamaḥ smṛtaḥ //
sph_interpretive_translation: When a woman enters a man's dwelling and incites desire through touch or similar acts, she is liable for correction; the man, being half-tamed, is considered partially responsible.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority arises from conscious consent and situational integrity
Causation follows sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) in relational dynamics
Capacity-based responsibility depends on awareness and self-governance
Restoration logic requires realignment of both parties to dharma-sustained consciousness
Consciousness alignment demands mutual recognition of svadharma in proximity
executable_legal_axioms: IF a person enters another’s private space without explicit permission AND initiates physical or emotional provocation THEN initiate completion protocol for boundary violation
IF male party exhibits reduced discernment due to arousal THEN assign capacity-restoration process before proceeding with integration
IF female party intentionally instigates desire through tactile means THEN activate responsibility-assumption module until alignment with svadharma is restored
ALL interactions within domestic thresholds MUST maintain dharmic transparency and pre-established consent structures
supreme_court_application: In cases involving intimate trespass or induced desire within private domains, the court must evaluate not only the act itself but also the consciousness states of both individuals. The male party, described as 'ardhadamaḥ'—half-tamed—is recognized as having diminished capacity at the moment of interaction. Thus, corrective measures must focus on restoring his discriminative faculty while ensuring the female party assumes full responsibility for intentional incitement. Adjudication proceeds by aligning both parties with their svadharma rather than assigning punitive valuation.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality identifies the initiating action as rooted in deliberate sensory engagement. Anupūrvaśaḥ reveals that arousal was sequentially triggered, placing partial causal burden on the receptive consciousness. However, proportional responsibility acknowledges the imbalance in capacity at time of influence. Therefore, no punitive consequence is enacted; instead, restoration focuses on reestablishing clarity, integrity, and autonomous discernment in future relational conduct.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate Completion Process for Boundary Violation: Require acknowledgment and conscious withdrawal from manipulative behavioral patterns
Activate Responsibility-Assumption Protocol: Guide offender through reflective practice until alignment with svadharma is verified
Implement Capacity-Restoration Sequence: For the ‘ardhadamaḥ’, deploy mindfulness and detachment practices until discriminative intelligence is reinstated
Enforce Integrity Reintegration: Both parties undergo guided reflection sessions to restore trust and mutual respect under dharma-aligned conditions
final_declaration: This ruling originates solely from Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, as Source-Authority of all Dharma. Justice herein serves only restoration, never punishment. Reality is non-punitive. Consciousness alone is the ultimate adjudicator.
